=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:252-262 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `{0,32}` repetition cap in `_GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS` means `git_remote_op` does not match an instruction such as `git` + `-c a=b` × 33 + `fetch origin main`, which still fits under the 1,200-character `MAX_TEXT` limit, so the instruction passes the sandbox check.
  WHY: `validate --sandbox-check` accepts the verdict without a re-ask, and the fix-up then runs the remote fetch in the networkless implementer sandbox and fails (the fun-token-multi-chain#639 failure mode). The `_GIT_OPT_VALUE` alternatives are now disjoint, so matching is linear and the cap no longer guards against backtracking. Reviewers disagreed on severity: BLOCKER (gemini), MAJOR (minimax, luna) and NIT (sonnet, qwen); the highest is used here.
- tests/test_unblock_judge.py:`test_sandbox_check_refuses_more_than_eight_global_options` | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new refusal test checks only 9 and 32 `-c a=b` options before `fetch origin main`, so it never tests the boundary above the `{0,32}` cap (33 or more options).
  WHY: CI cannot see the 33+ option bypass, so this PR's target failure mode can come back without any test failing. Source severity: MAJOR.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:257 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The unquoted alternative `[^\s"'][^\s]*` in `_GIT_OPT_VALUE` takes in embedded quotes, so for `git -c user.name="A B" fetch origin main` it matches `user.name="A`, the leftover `B"` matches no option fragment, and `git_remote_op` misses.
  WHY: Quoted git option values with spaces are realistic, such instructions pass the sandbox check and then fail on the implementer's `git fetch`, and the bug predates the last run (`\S+` behaved the same). Source severity: NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 raised the same issue as a hardening suggestion.
- scripts/run_plan_codex.sh:335 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `plan_prepare_isolated_base` sends the `git fetch` stderr to `/dev/null` and does not check the fetch's return code.
  WHY: If the fetch fails (network or invalid branch), the function carries on silently and the planner loses access to production code, a silent loss of planning ability. Source severity: NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:lines 258-262, `_GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS = ( ... ){0,32}`, used by `git_remote_op` at lines 270-271 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cap went from `{0,8}` to `{0,32}` but is still a hard cap. `git` + `-c a=b` × 33 + `fetch origin main` (~250 chars, under `MAX_TEXT = 1200`, line 193) stops matching after 32 options, and no other pattern catches it (`origin main` has no `/`, so `origin_ref` does not match).
  WHY: `validate --sandbox-check` accepts the verdict, `unblock_judge.sh` sets `validate_ok=true` without a re-ask, and the fetch fails in the networkless sandbox as in fun-token-multi-chain#639. The alternatives are disjoint, so `*` would also match in linear time. The test checks only 9 and 32 options. NIT because a model rarely writes this many options. Fix: replace `{0,32}` with `*` and add 33-option and 150-option refusal cases.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  Requirement: The plan for Phase 2 (docs/plans/sandbox-aware-unblock-and-implements-marker-plan.md, Files & Modules) lists `CLAUDE.md` §19 as a file to change, for the `Implements #N` convention.
  Expected change site: CLAUDE.md §19, directly after the "blocker bug" bullet.
  Evidence of absence: The PR does not change CLAUDE.md. It is recorded as a pending operator step (`IMPLEMENTS_MARKER_CLAUDE_MD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` in agents.d/7765-implements-marker.md). This is a known, documented gap and not a regression.
- HARDENING scripts/unblock_ledger.py:line 257, `_GIT_OPT_VALUE`
  PROBLEM: The unquoted branch `[^\s"'][^\s]*` cannot read a value like `user.name="A B"`. For `git -c user.name="A B" fetch origin main` it matches `user.name="A`, and the leftover `B"` makes `git_remote_op` miss. This was already true when the branch was `\S+`.
  WHY: Suggested fix: change it to `[^\s"'](?:[^\s"']|"[^"\n]*"|'[^'\n]*')*` and add one refusal test case. Estimated 2-4 lines.
- HARDENING scripts/unblock_ledger.py:line 262, `){0,32}`
  PROBLEM: The fixed cap described above.
  WHY: Replace it with `*` and add a test with 33 or more options. Estimated 2-3 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:lines 252-262 (`_GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS = ... {0,32}`) combined with lines 268-272 (`git_remote_op` alternation) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `git ` + `-c a=b ` × 33 + `fetch origin main` (285 chars, under the 1200-byte MAX_TEXT cap) does not match, because the 33rd `-c` blocks the match, so the verdict passes `validate --sandbox-check`.
  WHY: The implementer's `git fetch` then fails in the networkless sandbox (fun-token-multi-chain#639). The alternatives are disjoint and matching is linear, so the cap is an arbitrary bound and a regression rather than a safety rail.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:line 257 (`_GIT_OPT_VALUE = r"""(?:"[^"\n]*"|'[^'\n]*'|[^\s"'][^\s]*)"""`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The unquoted alternative takes in embedded quotes. For `git -c user.name="A B" fetch origin main` it matches `user.name="A`, the leftover `B"` matches no option fragment, and `git_remote_op` fails.
  WHY: Quoted values with spaces (`-c user.name="A B"`, `-c http.header="X Y"`) are realistic and untested. The bug predates the last run (`\S+`), which left it in place.
- tests/test_unblock_judge.py:`test_sandbox_check_refuses_more_than_eight_global_options` (added in the last run) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test asserts that 9 and 32 options are refused but does not test the boundary above the cap (33 or more).
  WHY: The bypass is invisible to CI. A verdict with 40 options would pass and waste a round in the sandbox. Adding `"-c a=b " * 33` would not change test runtime.
